events.title: Alphabet AI capex guidance update
events.why_it_matters: Alphabet's AI infrastructure spending is a bellwether for the entire AI capex cycle, influencing suppliers, cloud pricing, and tech valuations.
events.what_to_watch: Capex guidance vs. consensus, cloud growth acceleration, AI monetization signals, and any commentary on data center utilization.
sources: Web search: Alphabet AI capex 2026 guidance

events.title: Walmart Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Walmart's results provide a key read on US consumer health, inflation pass-through, and e-commerce growth, with broad market implications.
events.what_to_watch: Same-store sales growth, e-commerce growth rate, gross margin, inventory levels, and FY2027 guidance.
sources: Web search: Walmart Target earnings August 2026

events.title: Target Q2 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Target's earnings will signal discretionary spending trends and the health of the US middle-class consumer, a key driver of economic momentum.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable sales, traffic trends, margin recovery, inventory management, and any updates on tariff-related cost pressures.
sources: Web search: Walmart Target earnings August 2026

events.title: July CPI report
events.why_it_matters: The single most market-moving scheduled data point in the window, directly shaping Fed rate expectations and inflation narrative.
events.what_to_watch: Headline and core CPI prints versus consensus, and the market's implied Fed path reaction.

events.title: July PPI report
events.why_it_matters: Producer inflation feeds into Fed policy expectations and margin outlooks.
events.what_to_watch: Core PPI and pipeline price pressures feeding into CPI.

events.title: July Retail Sales
events.why_it_matters: Key read on US consumer health ahead of Walmart and Target earnings.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales and whether consumer spending is holding up.

events.title: University of Michigan sentiment (Aug prelim)
events.why_it_matters: Inflation-expectations component is a closely watched Fed input.

events.title: Weekly jobless claims
events.why_it_matters: High-frequency labor market signal feeding Fed policy expectations.
events.what_to_watch: Trend in initial and continuing claims for labor softening.

events.title: JOLTS (June)
events.why_it_matters: Labor demand indicator watched by the Fed for wage and tightness signals.
events.what_to_watch: Job openings and quits rate for labor market cooling.

events.title: Housing starts/permits (July)
events.why_it_matters: Housing sector health and rate sensitivity signal.
events.what_to_watch: Permit and start trends amid mortgage rate environment.

events.title: EIA weekly crude inventories
events.why_it_matters: Weekly crude and product inventory data moves oil prices.

top_risks: AI capex overbuild leading to a sharp correction in tech valuations if Alphabet signals reduced returns on investment
US consumer slowdown if Walmart or Target report weak guidance, suggesting broader economic deceleration
Tariff-driven margin compression in retail sector, potentially triggering earnings downgrades
top_opportunities: AI infrastructure suppliers and semiconductor names if Alphabet raises capex guidance above expectations
Retail sector value plays if Walmart/Target beat and raise, indicating resilient consumer spending
Cloud and AI software names on positive monetization commentary from Alphabet
summary: The near-term event landscape is dominated by upcoming retail earnings from Walmart and Target, which will provide critical signals on US consumer health and tariff impacts, and by Alphabet's AI capex guidance, a key driver for tech sector sentiment. Markets face moderate uncertainty as these data points could either reinforce or challenge current growth and inflation narratives.

catcher.coverage_assessment: The primary scan covered only three mega-cap earnings events and completely omitted the entire macro data calendar, the FOMC cycle, and all government/regulatory actions. Its coverage is extremely narrow for a two-week window.
catcher.biggest_gap: The July CPI report (expected ~Aug 12) — the most market-moving scheduled event in the window, entirely absent from the primary scan. Government actions could not be assessed because the web search tool returned empty results for all queries.
